findings.title: Fallback metadata query runs outside prompt suppression and without UIFail, including on the locked-keychain path
findings.snippet: guard SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &result) == errSecSuccess, let ref = result else {
findings.source: A scheduled refresh reaches readData (KeychainCredentialReader.swift:156-166). The suppressed direct read fast-fails with -25308/-25293. That also happens when the item's keychain has been locked since the target was bound (resolvedTarget skips the suppressed candidateMatches search once target is set).
findings.sink: KeychainCredentialReader.swift:218. An unsuppressed SecItemCopyMatching (kSecMatchItemList + kSecReturnRef) runs with no kSecUseAuthenticationUI key, called from readViaSecurityTool at line 187.
findings.description: Every other Keychain call in the component is wrapped in KeychainPromptSuppressor.withPromptsSuppressed and passes kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail. itemKeychain does neither, and the suppressor's resting state is interaction ALLOWED (exit() applies true at depth 0). This query runs specifically after an ACL/locked fast-fail, which is exactly when the item's keychain may be locked. On classic file keychains, looking up an item in a locked keychain while interaction is allowed can raise the SecurityAgent unlock dialog. That breaks the hard rule that scheduled reads never prompt, and the isUnlocked guard runs only after this call.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) The app binds the Claude credential target while the login keychain is unlocked. 2) The login keychain auto-locks (sleep or lock timeout). 3) The next 300 s scheduled refresh does a suppressed read, which fast-fails, and then calls itemKeychain with prompts enabled. 4) securityd may show an 'unlock keychain' password dialog on behalf of an LSUIElement app with no visible window. The refresh stalls, and the user learns to type their login password into unexplained prompts.
preconditions: Direct read already fast-fails (ad-hoc/unauthorized build or locked keychain)
Target identity already bound from an earlier successful search
securityd raises unlock UI for a ref lookup in a locked file keychain (not verified here)
findings.impact: An unrequested Keychain password or unlock prompt can appear outside the Authorize flow, and the refresh cycle can freeze behind it. This is defense in depth. No credential is disclosed.
findings.fix: Run the itemKeychain query inside KeychainPromptSuppressor.withPromptsSuppressed and add kSecUseAuthenticationUI: kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail, the same as exactQuery and candidateMatches. Or take the SecKeychainItem ref from the already-suppressed candidateMatches result and cache it with the TargetIdentity, so no new lookup is needed on the fallback path.
findings.evidence: KeychainCredentialReader.swift:211-218: the query dict has no kSecUseAuthenticationUI and the call is not wrapped. KeychainPromptSuppressor.swift:111-119: the depth-0 state applies setInteractionAllowed(true). KeychainCredentialReader.swift:187: itemKeychain runs before Self.isUnlocked(keychain). Compare KeychainAccessAuthorizer.swift:234-239 (candidateMatches, suppressed + UIFail) and KeychainCredentialReader.swift:254-266 (exactQuery, suppressed + UIFail).
